The Can package exercises comparison logic over inert records with a typed example, and lifecycle operations wait for a QD1-driven fixture need.

N holds observer state after P14; until then each operation fails loudly. The Can package tracks I01 (vocabularies, per-operation wrappers, roundtrip example). Absent a resident double, the merge cannot be confused with the QD1 qualified flow, and all behavior defers to the qualified owner.

i13_db_merge_shape.instructions: Select the merge shape for the K22 raw DB observer and K23 RETURNING observer across the sealed catalogue, checker, runtime adapter, and ordinary Can surface. The I13 card demands a catalogue.json delta plus a Can helper package with a typed example. The pair are pure in-memory doubles: no live databases, drivers, or sockets; digest-only namespace receipts; pinned identity-bound connections; single conversations; lexeme-exact numbers; code-unit-exact text; byte-exact bytes; null distinguished from empty text, empty bytes, and zero; stable row order; RETURNING payload-versus-final comparison; layered failures always naming engine, driver, or sql. The K22 normative independence scope forbids the observer from importing, calling, or reading adapter code, values, or state: adapter claims are verified AGAINST observer facts, and the observer never sources a fact FROM an adapter claim. QD1 intends Can driving C RETURNING while verifying independent final rows on PG/SQLite legs. The ship boundary compels ports rather than imports into runtime/. P14 is blocked, hence provisional status and zero execution credit for any choice.
